question: Pommel Horse, Roman Rings, Vaulting Table are few term which are related to__________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gymnastics.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pommel Horse, the Roman Rings (still rings) and the Vaulting Table are all apparatus used in artistic gymnastics. (जिम्नास्टिक्स)

◦ Pommel horse and rings are men's apparatus; the vaulting table is used by both men and women.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Men's artistic gymnastics has six apparatus: floor exercise, pommel horse, rings, vault, parallel bars and horizontal bar.

• Women's artistic gymnastics has four: vault, uneven bars, balance beam and floor exercise.

• The world governing body is the International Gymnastics Federation (FIG), founded in 1881, the oldest international sports federation.

NOTE

• India's best-known gymnast is Dipa Karmakar, who finished fourth in the vault at the 2016 Rio Olympics performing the difficult Produnova vault.

question: 'The Zoya Factor' is a novel written by _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anuja Chauhan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Zoya Factor" (2008) is a popular novel written by the Indian author Anuja Chauhan. It tells the story of an advertising executive who is believed to bring luck to the Indian cricket team. (अनुजा चौहान)

◦ It was adapted into a Hindi film in 2019 starring Sonam Kapoor and Dulquer Salmaan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other novels by Anuja Chauhan: "Battle for Bittora", "Those Pricey Thakur Girls", "The House That BJ Built" and "Baaz".

• Jerry Pinto wrote "Em and the Big Hoom"; Suketu Mehta wrote "Maximum City: Bombay Lost and Found"; Rajashree wrote "Trust Me".

NOTE

• Anuja Chauhan worked for many years in advertising and is credited with famous slogans such as "Yeh Dil Maange More" and "Mera Number Kab Aayega".

question: Hornbill festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hornbill Festival is celebrated every year from 1 to 10 December in Nagaland, at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama, near Kohima. (हॉर्नबिल महोत्सव — नागालैंड)

◦ It is called the "Festival of Festivals" because all the major Naga tribes take part in it together.

◦ It is named after the hornbill bird, which appears in the folklore of most Naga tribes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The festival was started in 2000 by the Government of Nagaland to encourage inter-tribal interaction and promote cultural heritage and tourism.

• Nagaland was created as a state in 1963; its capital is Kohima and its largest city is Dimapur.

NOTE

• Other tribal/state festivals: Bihu (Assam), Losar (Ladakh/Arunachal), Wangala (Meghalaya), Sangai Festival (Manipur), Pongal (Tamil Nadu).

question: Which of the following articles of the Indian constitution is related to "Uniform civil code for the citizen"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 44.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 44 of the Indian Constitution states that the State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) throughout the territory of India. (अनुच्छेद 44 — समान नागरिक संहिता)

◦ It is a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) contained in Part IV of the Constitution and is therefore not enforceable by any court.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 41 — right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases.

• Article 42 — provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.

• Article 43 — living wage, etc., for workers.

• Goa has long had a common civil code, and Uttarakhand became the first state in independent India to enact a UCC law (2024).

NOTE

• DPSPs are borrowed from the Irish Constitution. Other important DPSPs: Article 40 (organisation of village panchayats), Article 47 (raising the level of nutrition and prohibition of intoxicating drinks), Article 48A (protection of environment and wildlife).

question: Which are the most widespread forests in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tropical Deciduous Forests.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tropical Deciduous Forests, also called Monsoon Forests, are the most widespread forests of India. They occur in regions receiving 70–200 cm of rainfall and cover the largest area of the country. (पर्णपाती / मानसूनी वन)

◦ The trees shed their leaves for about six to eight weeks in the dry summer season.

◦ Important species: teak (sagwan), sal, sandalwood, shisham, mahua, neem, bamboo, khair.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• They are divided into moist deciduous (100–200 cm rainfall — eastern MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand, eastern slopes of the Western Ghats) and dry deciduous (70–100 cm — parts of UP, Bihar, MP, Maharashtra, Karnataka).

• Tropical Evergreen Forests grow where rainfall exceeds 200 cm (Western Ghats, Andaman and Nicobar, north-east India) and never shed all their leaves together.

• Mangrove (tidal) forests grow in coastal deltas, the largest being the Sundarbans delta of the Ganga-Brahmaputra.

NOTE

• As per the India State of Forest Report, the forest and tree cover of India is roughly 25% of its geographical area; Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest area and Mizoram the highest percentage of forest cover.

question: Nepal, a neighbouring country of India, is located to the ______ of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is North.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nepal, a landlocked Himalayan country, lies to the north of India, along the northern border shared with the Indian states of Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Sikkim. (नेपाल — भारत के उत्तर में)

◦ Its capital is Kathmandu and its currency is the Nepalese Rupee.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India shares land borders with seven countries: Bangladesh (longest, about 4,096 km), China, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan and Afghanistan.

• Nepal shares a border of roughly 1,751 km with India and also borders China (Tibet) in the north.

• Mount Everest (Sagarmatha, 8,849 m), the world's highest peak, lies on the Nepal–China border.

NOTE

• Sri Lanka lies to the south of India (separated by the Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar); Pakistan and Afghanistan lie to the north-west; Myanmar and Bangladesh to the east.

question: Mrinalini Sarabhai who received 'Padma Shri' in the year 1965 was a recognized ________ dancer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mrinalini Sarabhai (1918–2016) was a celebrated Indian classical dancer trained chiefly in Bharatanatyam (and also in Kathakali). She received the Padma Shri in 1965 and the Padma Bhushan in 1992. (मृणालिनी साराभाई — भरतनाट्यम)

◦ She founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad in 1949.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• She was the wife of the eminent scientist Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the father of the Indian space programme, and the mother of the dancer Mallika Sarabhai.

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni.

NOTE

• The eight recognised classical dance forms are Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of Millets or coarse grains?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wheat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Wheat is a fine cereal (a major food grain), not a millet. Jowar (sorghum), Bajra (pearl millet) and Ragi (finger millet) are the principal millets or coarse grains of India. (गेहूँ मोटा अनाज नहीं है)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Jowar is the third most important food crop by area and production; it is a rain-fed crop mostly grown in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana.

• Bajra grows well on sandy and shallow black soils; leading producers are Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Gujarat.

• Ragi is rich in iron, calcium and other micronutrients; Karnataka is the leading producer.

• Wheat is the main rabi crop, grown chiefly in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Haryana.

NOTE

• On India's proposal, the United Nations declared 2023 as the International Year of Millets; millets are promoted as "Shree Anna" for their nutritional value and climate resilience.

question: In Table Tennis, the length of upper surface of the table is __________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is 274 cm.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the rules of the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF), the playing surface of a table tennis table measures 274 cm (2.74 m) in length and 152.5 cm (1.525 m) in width, and it stands 76 cm above the floor. (टेबल टेनिस टेबल की लंबाई — 274 सेमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The net is 15.25 cm high, and the ball has a diameter of 40 mm, weighing about 2.7 g.

• A game is won by the player who first scores 11 points with a lead of at least 2 points; matches are usually best of 5 or 7 games.

• The ITTF was founded in 1926; table tennis became an Olympic sport at Seoul 1988.

NOTE

• Indian table tennis stars: Achanta Sharath Kamal, Manika Batra, Sathiyan Gnanasekaran and G. Sathiyan. Sharath Kamal received the Khel Ratna award in 2022.

question: Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni, raided which famous Indian temple?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Somnath Temple, Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahmud of Ghazni raided and plundered the famous Somnath Temple in Gujarat (Saurashtra/Prabhas Patan) in 1025–26 CE, in what was the last and most infamous of his seventeen raids on India. (सोमनाथ मंदिर — महमूद गजनवी)

◦ The Somnath temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is considered the first of the twelve Jyotirlingas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mahmud ruled Ghazni (Afghanistan) from 998 to 1030 CE and belonged to the Yamini/Ghaznavid dynasty; he assumed the title "Sultan".

• His court was adorned by Firdausi, author of the Shahnama, and Al-Beruni, author of "Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind)", who came to India with him.

• The Somnath temple was rebuilt several times; the present structure was completed in 1951 at the initiative of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

NOTE

• Mahmud's raids were mainly for plunder, not for empire-building in India; permanent Turkish rule began later with Muhammad Ghori and the Battle of Tarain (1192).

question: Wood's dispatch sent by the Court of Directors of the East India Company in 1854 was related to __________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Education.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Wood's Despatch (1854), sent by Sir Charles Wood, President of the Board of Control, to the Governor-General Lord Dalhousie on behalf of the Court of Directors of the East India Company, dealt with education in India. (वुड का डिस्पैच — शिक्षा से संबंधित)

◦ It is called the "Magna Carta of English Education in India".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Main recommendations of Wood's Despatch:

◦ Creation of a Department of Public Instruction in each of the five provinces.

◦ Establishment of universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras (set up in 1857 on the model of the University of London).

◦ A graded system of schools — vernacular primary schools, Anglo-vernacular high schools and affiliated colleges.

◦ Promotion of vernacular languages, grants-in-aid to private schools, teacher training and women's education.

NOTE

• Other landmarks: Macaulay's Minute (1835) favouring English education, the Hunter Commission (1882), the Indian Universities Act (1904) and the Sadler Commission (1917).

question: In India, National Voters' Day is celebrated on __________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is 25 January.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National Voters' Day (Rashtriya Matdata Diwas) is celebrated every year on 25 January, the foundation day of the Election Commission of India (established on 25 January 1950). (राष्ट्रीय मतदाता दिवस — 25 जनवरी)

◦ It has been observed since 2011 to encourage young citizens who turn 18 to enrol as voters.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body established under Article 324. It consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.

• The first Chief Election Commissioner of India was Sukumar Sen.

• The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years.

NOTE

• Other days in January: National Youth Day — 12 January (birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda), Army Day — 15 January, Republic Day — 26 January.

question: In June 2022, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has released a report titled __________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Payments Vision 2025.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2022, the Reserve Bank of India released the document "Payments Vision 2025", with the core theme "E-Payments for Everyone, Everywhere, Everytime (4Es)". (पेमेंट्स विजन 2025)

◦ Its goal is to make India's payment systems safe, secure, fast, convenient, accessible and affordable.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Payments Vision 2025 is built on five "anchor goalposts": Integrity, Inclusion, Innovation, Institutionalisation and Internationalisation.

• Among its targets were a three-fold increase in digital payment transactions and expanding UPI, RuPay and NEFT/RTGS acceptance abroad.

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 on the recommendation of the Hilton Young Commission and was nationalised in 1949. Its headquarters is in Mumbai.

NOTE

• RBI also launched the Digital Rupee (e-Rupee / CBDC) pilots in 2022 — the wholesale pilot on 1 November 2022 and the retail pilot on 1 December 2022.

question: Giorgia Meloni recently become first Woman Prime Minister of which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Italy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Giorgia Meloni became the first woman Prime Minister of Italy in October 2022, leading the "Brothers of Italy (Fratelli d'Italia)" party. (जॉर्जिया मेलोनी — इटली की पहली महिला प्रधानमंत्री)

◦ She succeeded Mario Draghi, the former President of the European Central Bank.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Italy — capital Rome; currency Euro; Italy is a member of the G7, G20, NATO and the European Union.

• The world's first woman Prime Minister was Sirimavo Bandaranaike of Sri Lanka (1960); India's first was Indira Gandhi (1966).

NOTE

• Vatican City, the smallest country in the world, and San Marino are enclaves within Italy. Famous Italian landmarks include the Colosseum, the Leaning Tower of Pisa and Mount Vesuvius.

question: Lucknow Pact was signed between ______.
option_1: the Muslim League and Mahatma Gandhi
option_2: the Indian National Congress and Arya Samaj
option_3: the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League
option_4: the Indian National Congress and Sayyid Ahmed Khan
solution_text:
The correct answer is the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League, signed at the Lucknow session of the Congress. (लखनऊ समझौता, 1916)

◦ It marked Hindu-Muslim unity in the national movement and also the reunion of the Moderates and the Extremists, who had split at the Surat session in 1907.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Key figures: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Annie Besant, Muhammad Ali Jinnah (then called the "Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity") and Ambica Charan Mazumdar, who presided over the Lucknow session.

• Under the pact, the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims, and both bodies jointly demanded self-government (Swaraj) for India.

• Separate electorates had first been granted by the Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act), 1909.

NOTE

• Sir Sayyid Ahmad Khan (1817–1898), founder of the Aligarh Movement and the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College (1875), died long before 1916, so he could not have been a party to this pact.

question:
Identify the Indian music personality.

Under him the shehnai came out of its ceremonial context and began to be acknowledged as a classical music instrument.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Bismillah Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916–2006) was the maestro who brought the shehnai out of its restricted ceremonial and wedding use and established it as a serious classical concert instrument. (उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खाँ — शहनाई)

◦ He played the shehnai from the ramparts of the Red Fort on 15 August 1947, India's first Independence Day.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, becoming only the third musician (after M. S. Subbulakshmi and Pandit Ravi Shankar) to receive the honour, along with the Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.

• He was closely associated with the city of Varanasi (Kashi).

NOTE

• Instrument maestros: Alla Rakha — tabla; Pandit Ram Narayan — sarangi; Ustad Bundu Khan — sarangi; Pandit Ravi Shankar — sitar; Ustad Amjad Ali Khan — sarod; Pandit Hari Prasad Chaurasia — flute; Ustad Zakir Hussain — tabla.

question: An image which can be obtained on a screen is called a __________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is real image.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "real image" is formed when light rays actually meet (converge) after reflection or refraction, and it can be obtained/caught on a screen. (वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब)

◦ A real image is always inverted with respect to the object.

◦ Examples: the image formed on a cinema screen, the image formed by a concave mirror or a convex lens when the object is beyond the focus.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A "virtual image" is formed when rays only appear to meet; it cannot be taken on a screen and is always erect. Examples: the image in a plane mirror, and the images formed by a convex mirror and a concave lens (always virtual, erect and diminished).

• "Vector image" is a computer-graphics term, and "spectral image" relates to spectroscopy — neither is an optics term for this definition.

NOTE

• Mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f; lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f; magnification m = h'/h = v/u (mirrors) and m = v/u (lenses). Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors because they give a wide, erect, virtual image.

question: In biology, the term "IVF" stands for __________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is In vitro fertilization.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• IVF stands for "In Vitro Fertilization" — the fertilisation of an egg by a sperm outside the body, in a laboratory dish, after which the embryo is transferred to the mother's uterus. (इन विट्रो फर्टिलाइजेशन — पात्रे निषेचन)

◦ "In vitro" is Latin for "in glass"; the resulting baby is popularly called a "test-tube baby".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The world's first test-tube baby, Louise Brown, was born in England in 1978; the technique was developed by Dr. Robert Edwards (Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, 2010) and Patrick Steptoe.

• India's first test-tube baby, Kanupriya (Durga), was born in Kolkata in 1978, credited to Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay.

• IVF is one of the Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART), regulated in India by the ART (Regulation) Act, 2021.

NOTE

• "In vitro" (in glass, in the lab) is the opposite of "in vivo" (within a living organism).

question: The leaves have a green pigment called _________ .which helps leaves to capture the energy from the sunlight.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chlorophyll.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chlorophyll" is the green pigment present in the chloroplasts of leaves; it absorbs sunlight and makes photosynthesis possible. (पर्णहरित / क्लोरोफिल)

◦ Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → (sunlight, chlorophyll) → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

◦ Chlorophyll contains magnesium (Mg) at the centre of its molecule.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Xanthophyll" is a yellow pigment and "carotene" an orange pigment; they become visible in autumn leaves when chlorophyll breaks down.

• "Cytoplasm" is the jelly-like substance inside a cell, not a pigment; a "cladophyll" is a flattened stem that looks and works like a leaf (as in Opuntia).

NOTE

• The chloroplast is called the "kitchen of the cell", while the mitochondrion is the "powerhouse of the cell". Photosynthesis takes place mainly in the mesophyll cells of the leaf.

question: Bhoota Kola, a spirit worship ritual dance is of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bhoota Kola" is a spirit (daiva) worship ritual dance performed in the Tulu Nadu region of coastal Karnataka (Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts) and adjoining parts of Kerala. (भूत कोला — कर्नाटक)

◦ The performer, believed to be possessed by the spirit or "daiva", dances through the night to the beat of drums, wearing elaborate costume and make-up.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bhoota Kola gained wide attention after the 2022 Kannada film "Kantara", which was based on this ritual.

• A similar ritual art in northern Kerala is "Theyyam".

• Other folk dances of Karnataka: Yakshagana, Dollu Kunitha, Veeragase, Kamsale and Huttari.

NOTE

• Folk dances to remember: Bihu (Assam), Garba (Gujarat), Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Ghoomar (Rajasthan), Lavani (Maharashtra), Chhau (Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal).

question: As the river enters the plain it get twists and turns forming large bends known as __________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is meanders.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a river enters the plains, it flows in large, looping bends called "meanders", formed because the river erodes the concave (outer) bank and deposits material on the convex (inner) bank. (विसर्प / मियेंडर)

◦ The word comes from the winding Meander (Menderes) river in Turkey.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• When a meander loop is cut off from the main channel, it forms a crescent-shaped "ox-bow lake".

• "Levees" are natural embankments of sediment built along the banks of a river during floods.

• A "stack" is a coastal landform — an isolated pillar of rock left standing in the sea after a sea arch collapses.

NOTE

• Depositional features of a river in its lower course: flood plains, levees, deltas, ox-bow lakes. Erosional features of the upper course: V-shaped valleys, gorges, waterfalls, potholes.

question: "Arthashastra" was written by _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chanakya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Arthashastra" was written by Chanakya, also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta, the chief minister and mentor of Chandragupta Maurya. (अर्थशास्त्र — चाणक्य)

◦ It is a treatise in Sanskrit on statecraft, economic policy, administration, taxation, diplomacy and military strategy, arranged in 15 books (adhikaranas).

◦ The text was rediscovered and published by R. Shamasastry in 1909.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Vishnu Sharma wrote the "Panchatantra"; Kalidasa wrote "Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghadutam, Raghuvamsham and Kumarasambhavam"; Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Mauryan Empire (322 BCE), not an author.

• Other sources for Mauryan history: Indica by Megasthenes, the Mudrarakshasa of Vishakhadatta and the edicts of Ashoka.

NOTE

• The Mauryan Empire (322–185 BCE) had its capital at Pataliputra; famous rulers were Chandragupta Maurya, Bindusara and Ashoka the Great.

question: The population of a nation in working age group is generally grouped between ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15 – 59 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The working age group (economically active population) of a nation is generally taken as 15 to 59 years. (कार्यशील आयु वर्ग — 15 से 59 वर्ष)

◦ Persons below 15 years and above 59 years are treated as the dependent population.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The age-sex structure of a population is shown by a population pyramid, with three broad groups: children (0–14), working age (15–59) and aged (60 and above).

• The dependency ratio = (dependent population ÷ working-age population) × 100.

• A large share of working-age people gives a country a "demographic dividend", which India is currently experiencing.

NOTE

• As per Census 2011, India's population was about 121 crore, sex ratio 943 females per 1000 males, literacy rate 74.04% and density 382 persons per sq km.

question: For a bank, the main liability is the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is deposits.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• For a bank, "deposits" are the main liability, because the money deposited by customers has to be repaid on demand and the bank pays interest on it. (जमा — बैंक की मुख्य देनदारी)

◦ In contrast, loans and advances given by a bank are its assets, since they bring interest income and are receivable by the bank.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Types of bank deposits: demand deposits (current and savings accounts, withdrawable on demand) and time/term deposits (fixed and recurring deposits).

• Banks must keep a part of these deposits as the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) with the RBI and another part as the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) in liquid assets.

• The DICGC insures bank deposits up to Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank.

NOTE

• "Economic rent" is a payment to a factor of production over and above its transfer earnings — a concept of economics, not a banking liability.

question: Which Mughal Emperor has attempted to vandalise the Kailash Temple at Ellora?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aurangzeb.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb (r. 1658–1707) is said to have attempted to destroy/vandalise the Kailash (Kailasa) Temple at Ellora, but the rock-cut temple proved too massive to be demolished. (औरंगज़ेब — कैलाश मंदिर, एलोरा)

◦ The Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) at Ellora, Maharashtra, is dedicated to Lord Shiva and was carved out of a single rock in the 8th century CE by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Ellora Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site with 34 caves — Buddhist, Hindu and Jain — showing India's religious harmony. The nearby Ajanta Caves are famous for their Buddhist paintings.

• Aurangzeb was the last of the "Great Mughals"; he reimposed the jizya in 1679 and was known for his orthodox religious policy.

NOTE

• Mughal rulers in order: Babur (1526), Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb, followed by the later Mughals up to Bahadur Shah Zafar (1857).
